title: GOODS-S field (NIRCam image)
caption: Part of the GOODS-South field, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, B. Robertson (UC Santa Cruz), B. Johnson (Center for Astrophysics, Harvard & Smithsonian), S. Tacchella (University of Cambridge, M. Rieke (Univ. of Arizona), D. Eisenstein (Center for Astrophysics, Harvard & Smithsonian), A. Pagan (STScI)

recognition.text: Published in the ESA/Webb image archive. No published rating.

story: More than 45,000 galaxies fill this infrared view of part of GOODS-South, a patch of sky that Hubble and other observatories have studied closely. The Webb image comes from JADES, the JWST Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey, one of the largest programs of the telescope's first year of science. It is set to use about 32 days of telescope time hunting for faint, distant galaxies.

Even with data still arriving, JADES has found hundreds of galaxies dating from the Universe's first 600 million years. There are far more of them than observations made before Webb's launch had predicted. That helps astronomers tackle the question of how the first stars and galaxies formed.

The team has also found galaxies from the Epoch of Reionization, when the Universe changed from opaque to transparent. Many show unusually strong emission lines because they are forming great numbers of hot, massive stars.

understand.summary: This Webb NIRCam image uses nine filters. Light at 0.9, 1.15 and 1.5 microns is shown in blue, light at 2.0, 2.77 and 3.35 microns in green, and light at 3.56, 4.1 and 4.44 microns in red.
understand.eye: Most of this light is infrared, invisible to the eye, and the galaxies are far too faint to see without a large telescope.
